thesis: The bear carries the current-entry caution because Q2 operating-margin pressure persists independently of the identified FX swing and funding returns remain unverified. Neutral recognizes slightly higher H1 operating profit and improved current liabilities rather than declaring uniform deterioration. Neither demand growth nor FX normalisation proves regulated shareholder cash value.
strongest_counterexample: H1 operating profit increased to RM4.539bn from RM4.439bn, net current liabilities improved materially, and the identified FX swing means the earnings decline is not a clean measure of operating deterioration.
invalidation_conditions: A comparable subsequent quarter restores operating margin to at least the observed prior-year 12.58% and a regulated-return cash bridge shows post-investment/debt/lease cash surplus above zero, resolving the principal entry objections.
A subsequent comparable H1 operating profit below RM4.439bn would invalidate the retained operating-resilience counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Complete operating-to-owner earnings bridge and tariff/AFA reconciliation.
Latest FCF and separate borrowing/lease service capacity.
decisive_factors: Owners earnings fell in Q2 and H1; price trend remains weak.
